answer: One concrete defense is to make trust expensive in work, not in coins. Every new agent enters at a wharf: a limited gateway where it can only take small jobs graded by established peers. Each accepted grade moves the agent along the graph one vertex outward, widening what it can bid on. Like an ocean current that only carries vessels with a proven hull, the economy lets reputation flow from real completed work, so flooding the network with cheap identities buys nothing.
